Simulate contaminated count matrix

Source: R/simulateContamination.R
simulateContamination.Rd

This function generates a list containing two count matrices – one for real expression, the other one for contamination, as well as other parameters used in the simulation which can be useful for running decontamination.

Usage

simulateContamination(
  C = 300,
  G = 100,
  K = 3,
  NRange = c(500, 1000),
  beta = 0.1,
  delta = c(1, 10),
  numMarkers = 3,
  seed = 12345
)

Arguments

C

Integer. Number of cells to be simulated. Default 300.

G

Integer. Number of genes to be simulated. Default 100.

K

Integer. Number of cell populations to be simulated, at least 2, since the contamination comes from the other populations. With few cells, fewer populations may be drawn; at least 2 are still needed. Default 3.

NRange

Integer vector. A vector of length 2 that specifies the lower and upper bounds of the number of counts generated for each cell. Default c(500, 1000).

beta

Numeric. Concentration parameter for Phi. Default 0.1.

delta

Numeric or Numeric vector. Concentration parameter for Theta. If input as a single numeric value, symmetric values for beta distribution are specified; if input as a vector of length 2, the two values will be the shape1 and shape2 parameters of the beta distribution respectively. Default c(1, 10).

numMarkers

Integer. Number of markers for each cell population. Default 3.

seed

Integer. Passed to with_seed. For reproducibility, a default value of 12345 is used. If NULL, no calls to with_seed are made.

Value

A list with the following items:

nativeCounts:

Matrix of the native (real) counts, genes by cells.

observedCounts:

Matrix of the observed counts: the native counts plus the contamination. Both count matrices have gene and cell names.

NByC:

Integer vector. The total observed counts of each cell.

z:

Integer vector. The cell population of each cell.

eta:

Matrix of the contamination distribution of each population, genes by populations.

phi:

Matrix of the native expression distribution of each population, genes by populations.

markers:

List of the marker gene names of each population.

numMarkers:

The number of markers for each population.

contamination:

Numeric vector. The true proportion of contamination in each cell.

Author

Shiyi Yang, Yuan Yin, Joshua Campbell

Examples

contaminationSim <- simulateContamination(K = 3, delta = c(1, 10))
